classification_reasons: Spec is tight now (Flagged concern on the inherited ZeroDivisionError message was closed by the owner 2026-09-22, acceptance is measurable including the exact-percentage case), but the change adds a brand-new function and brand-new tests rather than being covered by pre-existing tests, so the 'code the existing tests already cover' leg of routine does not hold.

Blast radius is small (3 source files, no risk-list item, no schema/contract change) but this is a feature change with two prior fix rounds (phase b round 1 on a formula defect, phase c round 1 on a plan_sync false-positive from the sandbox-masked .env), which is exactly the kind of history the framework treats as non-routine to keep the tighter iteration cap in force.
status.yaml already carries this classification through from phase b/c; nothing in phase (d)'s diff shrinks the blast radius or spec surface enough to downgrade it.
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's Proposed outcome against the shipped percent(part, whole) — return value, zero-whole ZeroDivisionError, export, and tests all match; found nothing solving a different problem.

Spec and plan: checked every Requirements line and both Open questions (reuse divide: yes; rounding: none) against calc.py/__init__.py/test_calc.py; the one Flagged concern (inherited 'b must not be zero' message) is marked closed with an owner decision dated 2026-09-22 and the code matches that decision. Diff touches exactly the three files plan.md's 'Files that change' lists, and the two build commits (4d78c1a, be93afd) land in the order plan.md's 'Order of work' specifies (steps 1+2 together, then step 3).

Proof: independently ran `python -m pytest -q` (5 passed) and `python -m ruff check .` (All checks passed!) myself from the repo root, not just read evidence/test.log and lint.log — outputs match. `python -m compileall -q .` was blocked by this session's own sandbox, but build was already gated green at phase (c) and test.log/verifier.md corroborate a clean compileall at phase (d) too. verifier.md shows direct calls (percent(1,4)=25.0, percent(7,100)=7.0 exact, percent(1,0) raises) rather than only re-quoting the plan, and explicitly confirms the exact-percentage regression from round 1 is fixed.

Blast radius: percent is additive, nothing else imports it yet; add/divide signatures and tests/test_flag.py are byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed by reading the current files). git diff main...HEAD touches no guardrail file (CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml, .claude/**) and no sdlc.yaml risk_list item applies. Working tree shows .env as 'modified', but git cat-file reports it as a character-special device (sandbox's read-deny mask over the real file), not a real content change, and fix-response.md documents this exact artifact was already investigated and cleared at phase (c)'s gate re-run (plan_sync false positive) — not a new finding, not part of this commit's diff, not read by me.

Policies: security-baseline and data-conventions correctly assessed as not applicable (pure arithmetic, no I/O, no schema); coding-standards followed (no docstring, matches file style, one function, no dead code); definition-of-done's three commands are green by independent re-run.

Tests: test_percent's two assertions (25.0 and the exact 7.0) cannot pass under the buggy divide(part, whole) * 100 ordering that round 1 shipped, so the test does pin the fix, not just the happy path; test_percent_zero_whole_raises pins the exception type independent of divide's implementation. Neither existing test (test_add, test_divide_by_zero_raises, test_flag.py) was touched or weakened.

Tried to break the implementation with inputs outside the acceptance set: negative part/whole, part > whole, floating imprecision on non-exact ratios (1/3) — all produce ordinary, unsurprising float behavior consistent with 'no rounding, raw float' and the divide-delegation error contract; found one pre-existing, already-disclosed nit (large |part| approaching 1.8e306 overflows to inf via part*100) that was raised and accepted as not-Important in the phase-(c) fix-response, not a new gap.
